brand_details.web_text_en: Screech Rum has been imported from Jamaica for over 200 years.  During that time, salt fish was being shipped to the West Indies in exchange for Rum.  This resulted in fish being a national dish for Jamaicans and Rum becoming a staple for Newfoundlanders.  A true part of Newfoundland’s tradition and culture was born and continues to today.  During the early days, they were not overly concerned with alcohol content.  The fisherman used to drink the Rum at a very high strength.  In the 20th century, the government took control of the liquor trade and put the rum in a sophisticated, unlabelled bottle and fortunately did not alter the rum itself.  This amazing product may have continued to be bottled unlabeled but as the story goes, a visiting American World War II serviceman downed the rum in one quick shot.  His screams of distress brought the attention of bystanders who heard him howl, “What the cripes was that ungodly Screech?!” As word of the incident spread, more soldiers began trying this mysterious rum and adopting it as their own.  The funny name stuck, and a legend was born.

brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: The history of Newfoundland has been described as "a long battle between rum and religion.”  In the early days, the fisherman used to drink the Rum at a very high strength being not too concerned with alcohol content which continued for generations.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Over two centuries ago fish was being shipped to the West Indies from the Newfoundland area in exchange for Rum.  This resulted in fish being a national dish for Jamaicans and Rum becoming a staple for Newfoundlanders.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: A traditional Newfoundland Screech Ceremony involves the kissing of a cod.  The kissing of a cod meant to wish one bon voyage for those who were sailing South and returning with the rum. Foreigners who do this are considered "Screeched In".

brand_details.name: Domaines Ott
brand_details.web_text_en: In 1896 Marcel Ott, a young Alsatian agronomist, fell in love with rosé and decided that it will be the wine that he will specialize in. After having traveled the length and breadth of France looking for the right terroir, he finds the perfect place in beautiful Provence, a region left severely destroyed by the phylloxera crisis. Undeterred by the challenge of starting from scratch, in 1912 he purchases Château de Selle, a 140-hectare (346-acre) property in Tarandeau, which was an old residence of the Earls of Provence. In 1936, he acquires Clos Mireille, a 170-ha (420-acre) property bordering the Mediterranean in La Londe-les-Maures. In 1956, the Ott family invests in a third domain, the 74-ha (183-acre) Domaine Romassan in Le Castellet, near Bandol. In 2004, the three domains are purchased by the Rouzaud family, owners of Roederer Champagne.  Under the new ownership, the wine range has been further expanded by adding the By Ott selection. The grapes are predominantly purchased, which allows for greater flexibility and growth. The wines are assembled in the new cellar at Château de Selle. The $11.65 million cellar is composed of solid stone blocks, specifically placed to create the impression of a giant porous screen and is completely gravity fed. It was commissioned by Frédéric Rouzaud and designed by Carl Fredrik Svenstedt, the architect responsible for the Louvre Museum extension in Paris.
brand_details.web_text_short_en: In 1896 Marcel Ott fell in love with rosé and decided that it will be the wine to specialize in. After having traveled all of France looking for the right terroir, he finds the perfect place in beautiful Provence. In 1912 he commenced the purchase of three outstanding plots within Provence which were cultivated, maintained and prospered through the generations that followed. In 2004, the three domains were purchased by Roederer Champagne.
brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: The land is nurtured without chemicals or any intensive production techniques.  All products that are used to treat common vine diseases are organically based treatments that are naturally occurring.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Generations of passed-on expertise are preserved with the utmost care and respect for what the environment continues to offer from vintage to vintage. Each harvest is carefully hand-picked and patiently sorted to the highest practices of quality.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Inspired by the three Domaines and their respective environments within Provence, rare and unique cuvees are expressed to sublime outcomes by always keeping true to nature's amazing offerings.  Each vintage radiates a different energy.

brand_details.web_text_en: In 1896 Marcel Ott, a young Alsatian agronomist, fell in love with rosé and decided that it will be the wine that he will specialize in. After having traveled the length and breadth of France looking for the right terroir, he finds the perfect place in beautiful Provence, a region left severely destroyed by the phylloxera crisis. Undeterred by the challenge of starting from scratch, in 1912 he purchases Château de Selle, a 140-hectare (346-acre) property in Tarandeau, which was an old residence of the Earls of Provence. In 1936, he acquires Clos Mireille, a 170-ha (420-acre) property bordering the Mediterranean in La Londe-les-Maures. In 1956, the Ott family invests in a third domain, the 74-ha (183-acre) Domaine Romassan in Le Castellet, near Bandol. In 2004, the three domains are purchased by the Rouzaud family, owners of Roederer Champagne.  Under the new ownership, the wine range has been further expanded by adding the By Ott selection. The grapes are predominantly purchased, which allows for greater flexibility and growth. The wines are assembled in the new cellar at Château de Selle. The $11.65 million cellar is composed of solid stone blocks, specifically placed to create the impression of a giant porous screen and is completely gravity fed. It was commissioned by Frédéric Rouzaud and designed by Carl Fredrik Svenstedt, the architect responsible for the Louvre Museum extension in Paris.

brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Inspired by the three Domaines and their respective environments within Provence, rare and unique cuvees are expressed to sublime outcomes by always keeping true to nature's amazing offerings.  Each vintage radiates a different energy.

brand_details.web_text_en:
The Louis Roederer champagne house has been creating wines for over two centuries. The house has remained an independent, family-owned company and is now managed by Frédéric Rouzaud, who represents the seventh generation of the lineage. They are one of the last independently owned Champagne houses. 
Louis Roederer II fashioned an exclusive champagne for the Tsar Alexander II of Russia and launched a novel concept: the very first Cuvée de Prestige. It was created in 1876 and named ‘Cristal’. Ever since, the elegance and grace of Cristal continues to forge Louis Roederer’s reputation for excellence.
The crafting of a fine champagne requires a slow rhythm, patience and restraint. Time is the ultimate luxury. The time to patiently blend components, to choose a better path, the time to share experience and work together towards the creation of outstanding champagnes from unique terroirs.

brand_details.web_text_en:
Masi Agricola represents a wine history dating back two and a half centuries to 1772, when the Boscaini family acquired the prestigious vineyards in the small valley called “Vaio dei Masi,” the origin of the company’s name. With resounding consistency and a passion for quality winemaking, the company is still in family hands, run by the sixth and seventh generations.
Rooted in Valpolicella Classica, Masi produces and distributes Amarone and other premium wines inspired by the values of the Venetian territories to more than 120 countries worldwide. Masi also produces wines from the historic Serego Alighieri estate in Valpolicella, the Bossi Fedrigotti Estate in Trentino, as well as owning the organically run estates of Poderi del Bello Ovile in Tuscany and Masi Tupungato in Argentina. In 2017, Masi acquired 60% of Canevel Spumante in Valdobbiadene, giving it a foothold in the heartland of Prosecco. 
A leader in the art of producing Amarone, Masi constantly innovates and passes on its expertise in the appassimento method, which has been practised since the time of the ancient Romans  Masi bases its own activities on social, ethical and environmental values. Care and respect for the environment are part of the Masi culture and philosophy.
The use of native grapes, indigenous winemaking methods and the continuing research and experimentation carried out by its progressive Technical Group, make Masi one of the most famous producers of high-quality Italian wines in the world.

vintage_details.winemaking_notes_en: Amarone is made using the ancient '"appassimento" (partial grape drying) method in use since Roman times. At the end of September/beginning of October the best bunches from the hillside vineyards are picked and laid out on traditional bamboo racks (“arele”) in special lofts where the natural drying process is controlled by the NASA system. By the middle of February the grapes have lost about 40% of their weight and have acquired great concentration. Of the grapes used, only the Corvina grape is subject to a slight natural attack of "botrytis" (noble rot). The Oseleta grapes confer greater tannic structure and deeper colour to the wine after drying. The grapes are pressed gently after partial destalking and fermented for 45 days in large Slavonian oak barrels or in stainless steel vats at ambient cellar temperatures. The final fermentation takes 35 days in 30-40 hectolitre barrels, induced by the inoculation of selected yeasts highly resistant to alcohol and the malolactic fermentation.   38-40 months in 600-litre Slavonian and Allier oak casks (1/3  new, 1/3 2nd passage, 1/3 3rd passage). Six months bottle ageing minimum.

Masi Agricola represents a wine history dating back two and a half centuries to 1772, when the Boscaini family acquired the prestigious vineyards in the small valley called “Vaio dei Masi,” the origin of the company’s name. With resounding consistency and a passion for quality winemaking, the company is still in family hands, run by the sixth and seventh generations.
Rooted in Valpolicella Classica, Masi produces and distributes Amarone and other premium wines inspired by the values of the Venetian territories to more than 120 countries worldwide. Masi also produces wines from the historic Serego Alighieri estate in Valpolicella, the Bossi Fedrigotti Estate in Trentino, as well as owning the organically run estates of Poderi del Bello Ovile in Tuscany and Masi Tupungato in Argentina. In 2017, Masi acquired 60% of Canevel Spumante in Valdobbiadene, giving it a foothold in the heartland of Prosecco. 
A leader in the art of producing Amarone, Masi constantly innovates and passes on its expertise in the appassimento method, which has been practised since the time of the ancient Romans  Masi bases its own activities on social, ethical and environmental values. Care and respect for the environment are part of the Masi culture and philosophy.
The use of native grapes, indigenous winemaking methods and the continuing research and experimentation carried out by its progressive Technical Group, make Masi one of the most famous producers of high-quality Italian wines in the world.

vintage_details.winemaking_notes_short_en: Amarone is the product of the ancient wine making method called "appassimento" (grape drying). At the end of September or beginning of October the best bunches are laid on bamboo racks in the old lofts of estate buildings where large windows provide natural ventilation. By the middle of February the grapes weigh 35-40% less. Only the Corvina grape is affected by botrytis ("noble rot"). The wine ferments for 48 days in large Slavonian oak.
vintage_details.winemaking_notes_en: Amarone is the product of the ancient wine making method called "appassimento" (grape drying). At the end of September or beginning of October the best bunches are laid on bamboo racks in the old lofts of estate buildings where large windows provide natural ventilation. By the middle of February the grapes weigh 35-40% less. Only the Corvina grape is affected by botrytis ("noble rot"). After a delicate pressing, the dried grapes, which are partially destalked, ferment for 48 days in large Slavonian oak barrels, at low, natural temperatures (the weather is very cold at this time of year); then the wine continues to ferment until the sugar has been totally transformed into alcohol and the malolactic fermentation takes place.  The wine is then matured for 3 years in Slavonian oak barrels of 6-20 hl, 4 months in cherry wood casks, then a minimum of 5 months in the bottle.

The particular terrain and climatic conditions permit only limited production, but of very high quality.

vintage_details.viticultural_notes_en: Within the Marlborough wine region, Waihopai River Vineyard lies on the flats on the right bank of the Waihopai River, at the mouth of the Waihopai Valley. By far the most substantial part of the 260ha vineyard is planted in Sauvignon Blanc.  What makes the Waihopai River Vineyard such a great place is the exceptional diversity across the one site. It consists of three terraces, formed by glacial movement over thousands of years.  The bottom terrace consists of the old river bed, with silt, silty clay loam and gravel soils. Diverging seams of varying soils give real diversity of flavours to work with. The middle terrace has more gutsy soil, with more fertile topsoil overlaying the gravels below. This area also gives a wide range of flavours and characteristics.  The top terrace is the largest of the three, and varies across its width from west to east. The soils from the west of the terrace are very similar to the mid-terrace, and as you go towards the Delta Hill, the soils get gradually deeper and richer, and in this area specifically, the shade that the hill provides adds to the variable conditions.

brand_details.web_text_en: Marisco Vineyards, home of world-renowned brands The Ned & The Kings Series, is located in the Waihopai Valley of Marlborough, New Zealand - a location which provides a near perfect environment for producing wines of startling character. Brent Marris, Proprietor and Chief Winemaker, grew up on some of the very first vineyards in Marlborough, planted by his father. As a young winemaker, he was responsible for the development of two major New Zealand wine brands.  Tapping into this deep well of knowledge, Brent selected several outstanding local sites as base for a venture to create his own family legacy, Marisco Vineyards. Marisco Vineyards was initially conceived in 2003 and the first wine The Ned Sauvignon Blanc was introduced in 2006.  These vineyards continue to flourish producing their core brands along with their targeted niche brands such as The Craft Series. They remain a progressive wine company committed to building brands and taking the unique Marlborough, New Zealand story of wine to the entire world.

brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: Driven by a love of winemaking, Brent Marris was the first Marlborough native to become a qualified winemaker.   After assisting to propel other major New Zealand wine brands, a new tradition was started with his own project of Marisco.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Upon an exceptional 268-hectare property on the banks of the Waihopai River in Marlborough, the spectacular planted fruit of the Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir thrive in this perfect climate.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Brent Marris researched his family tree in 2009 and found that his name derived from William de Marisco, a descendant of King Henry I. He promptly resurrected the original family name for the business and Marisco Vineyards was born.

brand_details.web_text_en: Two Rivers takes its name from the iconic Wairau and Awatere rivers of Marlborough. This is where Founder and winemaker David Clouston grow up, surrounded by these rivers, playing and then working amongst the vines in a fifth generation Marlborough farming family. David fell in love with his craft by osmosis really, realising early on how special this place was, unlike any other wine growing region. A terroir that creates wines, notably Sauvignon Blanc, with intensity, purity and when all elements are harnessed correctly, elegance. David spent many years making wines in France, Spain, Chile, America and Corsica before establishing Two Rivers back in Marlborough, New Zealand in 2004. David’s bold approach to winemaking and his desire to push boundaries, makes for distinctive and innovative wines for which Two Rivers is celebrated.

brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: David spent three vintages on the French island of Corsica, where he became passionate about pure, vibrant and dry rosé wines. Today his Two Rivers Isle of Beauty Rosé, named as a tribute to the island, is championing rosés around the world.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: In 2020 Two Rivers embarked on the organic conversion of their Brookby Hill Vineyard. Treading lightly on the land, increasing biodiversity and respecting the soil means that no synthetic chemical fertilisers, pesticides or herbicides are used.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Two Rivers winemaking techniques include natural fermentation, aging in concrete egg tanks, clay amphoras and an assortment of French oak cuves and barrels, as well as bottling wine unfined and unfiltered to retain complexity and texture.

vintage_details.winemaking_notes_en: Sourced grapes are vinified using the traditional Porto Wine method. Hand-picked grapes are softly crushed and, after partial stalk-removal, fermented with maceration allowing the best components of the grape skins to be extracted. The whole process takes place under strict control of both temperature and wine density, making it possible for the winemaker to choose the ideal moment for the addition of wine alcohol, fundamental to halt fermentation and keep Porto wine natural sweetness. The wines selected for the final blend of this reserve Porto wine stay in the Douro after the harvest and are taken to the company´s traditional Porto Wine lodges in V.N.Gaia the following Spring where they mature in oak casks. For several years the wines undergo numerous transfers, analyses and tasting that monitor the ageing of wines, preparation of blends, as well as refreshing and eventual adjustment when tasting so determines. The final blend is composed with wines from different ages and origins to achieve a consistency of style and quality typical of Porto Ferreira Dona Antónia Reserva Tawny. The selected wines usually varies between 4 and 12 years of age, achieving an average age of about 7 years.  Tawny ports are wines usually made from red grapes that are aged in wooden barrels exposing them to gradual oxidation and evaporation. As a result of this oxidation, they mellow to a golden-brown colour.

brand_details.web_text_en: Master of Wine Norrel Robertson oversees the creation of Anciano wines and conducts extensive tasting and analysis of the best cuvées available in collaboration with expert local winemakers. The oak aged Tempranillo wines come from Bodegas Navalón which is surrounded by the ancient vineyards of DO Valdepeñas in the rural heart of Spain. The bodega has been the passion of the same local family for several generations, originally founded at the start of the 20th Century by Don Juan Sánchez. Other wines including a young Garnacha come from the Mediterranean coast, near Valencia, and Anciano Old Vines Garnacha expresses the unique and dramatic terroir of Calatayud, in the northeastern region of Aragon.

brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: In the Spanish winemaking tradition, Anciano wines are matured both in oak barrels and in cellar to guarantee the perfect balance of flavours.  Great wines take time, so they are only released once they have reached the perfect level of maturity.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Anciano wines are crafted in the rural heartlands of Spain where the rugged landscapes, ancient soils and ideal climate provide the perfect conditions for growing vines that produce wines uniquely of Spanish character for the past centuries.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Each region has its own uniqueness.  From how the large stones soak up the sun’s rays in Valdepeñas to the gnarly old vines in Calatayud and to the fertile land in Terres dels Alforins.  These wines display the diversity found in the soils.

brand_details.web_text_short_en: Benromach Distillery was established in Forres, Scotland in 1898.  It was the realisation of a long-held dream for the Urquhart family when they acquired the distillery in 1993.  Five years of meticulous refitting of the distillery followed before officially reopening our doors in 1998.  Our whisky is handcrafted and reminiscent of a time when Speyside distilleries malted their own barley using peat to fuel the fires and impart a touch of smoke.
brand_details.web_carousel_header1_en: Made by Hand for Genuine Character
brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: A handful of distillers relying entirely on our expertise and senses to make the finest handmade whisky; with a subtly smoky character.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Good casks are crucial to creating a good whisky, and we get the most flavour from First-Fill oak casks. All of our casks are hand-filled, individually weighed, stencilled by hand and stowed in our traditional dunnage warehouses.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: It takes just four ingredients to create our whisky – locally sourced barley, water from the Chapelton Spring, brewers’ and distillers’ yeast and most importantly, the people.

brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Good casks are crucial to creating a good whisky, and we get the most flavour from First-Fill oak casks. All of our casks are hand-filled, individually weighed, stencilled by hand and stowed in our traditional dunnage warehouses.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: It takes just four ingredients to create our whisky – locally sourced barley, water from the Chapelton Spring, brewers’ and distillers’ yeast and most importantly, the people.

vintage_details.winemaking_notes_short_en: In this era of mergers and consolidations we go against the grain; an independent, Scottish owned and managed whisky company. We chose to step away from the corporate treadmill and short-term targets. Instead, we focus on the important things; making great whisky and enjoying life. GlenAllachie 12 year old is the heart of our range, a landmark bottling.

brand_details.web_text_short_en: One of Scotland’s few independently owned and managed distilleries, The GlenAllachie is led by industry veteran, Billy Walker, who boasts an almost 50-year tenure in whisky. Nestled at the foot of Ben Rinnes, the distillery lies at the heart of the Speyside, with a focus upon quality over quantity.  Spanning 16 on-site warehouses, our passionate team have complete control, giving them the freedom to make decisions for all the right reasons.
brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: Billy Walker, Trisha Savage and Graham Stevenson came together to acquire the GlenAllachie Distillery and form The GlenAllachie Distillers Company Limited, bringing with them over 100 years of industry knowledge and expertise.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: The GlenAllachie Distillery was the fourth distillery designed by William-Delme Evans and built by Mackinlay McPherson (distilling arm of Scottish and Newcastle). It was designed to be almost full gravity fed to run on reduced energy.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: GlenAllachie has a vast amount of aged stock dating as far back as the 1970’s. Having been given the gift of time, Master Distiller Billy Walker immediately set to work putting his fingerprint on our single malt.

vintage_details.viticultural_notes_short_en: A four-grain, high-rye straight bourbon whiskey with a mash bill of 65% corn, 22% rye, wheat and barley making up the rest. The copper column and copper pot-doubler distillation method creates a spirit full of flavor and texture. Then the spirit is aged for a minimum of 4 years in virgin American oak barrels with a deep char #4 on the staves and # 2 char on the barrel heads.

Planted on various Wente clones, which are all harvested and vinified separately, the variation within the vineyards adds to the complexity of the wine.

brand_details.name: Wente Family Estates
brand_details.web_text_en: Wente Vineyards is proud to be America’s longest, continuously operated family-owned winery which was founded in 1883 by C.H. Wente.  It uniquely survived the Prohibition era because the Catholic church bought a consistent supply of sacramental wine from Wente which had the proper licenses and deals in place with the Catholic church.  2,000 acres in Livermore, 1,000 in Monterey, whereby certified organic products are practices are managed in the vineyards today.   They were first to varietally label wines and first to plant Chardonnay with cuttings obtained from France.   A five-generation family legacy continues by preserving the traditional philosophy along with remaining true to their unique heritage.  A successful future awaits which celebrates the original culture of wine and each generation who made it.
brand_details.web_text_short_en: Founded 137 years ago, Wente Vineyards is the oldest, continuously operated family-owned winery in the United States. Located in the historic Livermore Valley, Wente Vineyards is recognized as one of California’s premier wine country destinations, featuring wine tasting, food and wine pairing, events and championship golf.
brand_details.web_carousel_text1_en: Founded in 1883, Wente Vineyards is currently owned and managed by the Fourth and Fifth Generations of the Wente Family. The family is known as California’s First Family of Chardonnay for being the first to plant Chardonnay in the state in 1912.
brand_details.web_carousel_text2_en: Wente Vineyards wines are 100% estate grown from vineyards in the historic Livermore Valley and Arroyo Seco, Monterey AVAs.  These climatically diverse growing areas are ideal for the varietals that Wente Vineyards specializes in.
brand_details.web_carousel_text3_en: Wente Vineyards is proud to be California Certified Sustainable in both their vineyards and winery. Currently, less than 4% of California wineries are certified in both their vineyards and winery. From vine to glass, sustainable practices throughout.

vintage_details.winemaking_notes_short_en: The wine is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon (78 %), Petite Sirah (19 %) and Petite Verdot (3 %); percentages slightly differ from each vintage.  Wine was pressed on the skins after 7-12 days.  Varietals were fermented separately in upright stainless steel fermenters and pumped over twice daily.  Aged for 16 months in a combination of French, American and neutral oak barrels as well as stainless steel tanks to add fruit vibrancy.
